person: New parent in the United States, partner/co-parent household
situation: A parent notices a foul smell coming from their newborn's umbilical cord area after 11 days and is alarmed, interpreting it as a sign of infection.
trigger: Smell observed during a diaper change at day 11 postpartum; parent immediately searches forums for 'smelly umbilical cord'.
context: Parent is already on edge; baby has had a previous fungal infection requiring antibiotics. The smell triggers alarm disproportionate to the normal pre-separation process.
behaviour: Posted to r/beyondthebump describing the smell
Kept the baby naked for several days hoping to aid drying
Sought reassurance from other parents online
constraint: No medical professional available at the moment; forum is the fastest source of reassurance.
thought: It smells like rotting flesh — something must be wrong. The cord should have fallen off by now.
fear: Serious infection requiring medical intervention; judgment for not catching it sooner.
emotional_stake: Guilt and fear amplified by the visceral nature of the smell.
exact_language: It smells like rotting flesh lol its on her blankets and clothes. I decided to keep her naked for a few days to help with the drying.
desired_change: Reassurance that smell is normal; clear timeline for when to worry vs when to wait.

evidence_source.excerpt: It smells like rotting flesh lol its on her blankets and clothes. I decided to keep her naked for a few days to help with the drying.
evidence_source.context: Parent posting about smell alarm at day 11; community reassured it was normal pre-separation.
